# THE LOCK. An exact freeze of `pip install '.[infra,tui,data,dev]'` in a fresh
# virtualenv on CPython 3.14.6 (Windows) --- the interpreter this harness is
# developed and tested on.
#
# pyproject.toml states what the harness *can* run against (ranges); this file
# states what it *has* run against (versions). They answer different questions
# and both are needed:
#
#     pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.txt
#     pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation -e .
#
# The first command verifies every downloaded artifact against this file. The
# second installs only this checkout and cannot resolve around the lock.
#
# Why a lock at all, for a research tool. The harness advertises bit-exact
# record/replay, and that is true of the LLM half only: prompts are hashed and
# completions are replayed from a trace. The numeric half had no such guarantee.
# A rolling statistic, an NaN convention or a float reduction order changing
# inside numpy/pandas/numba/vectorbt moves every metric in every ledger, and the
# harness has no way to notice -- the run simply reports different numbers and
# says nothing. Unbounded ">=" floors made that a matter of when, not if.
#
# Transitive packages are pinned too. numba's kernels and vectorbt's reductions
# are where the float order actually lives, and pinning only direct dependencies
# would leave llvmlite and scipy free to move underneath them.
#
# Regenerating: install `.[infra,tui,data,dev]` into a FRESH virtualenv, then
# `pip freeze --exclude-editable` it. Do not freeze a working environment -- this
# developer's interpreter carries ~150 packages (jupyter, streamlit, torch) the
# harness has never imported, and a lock is only worth having if every line in
# it is something the project actually resolves. Reading dependency metadata
# instead of installing is not equivalent either: it missed linkify-it-py and
# uc-micro-py, which reach textual through an extras-of-a-dependency
# (markdown-it-py[linkify,plugins]) that a naive marker walk evaluates away.
#
# NOT pinned, deliberately: anthropic and openai. Both are reached over the
# network and the offline suite uses the scripted/replay providers, so neither
# is installed in the reference environment -- there is no tested version to
# claim, and inventing one would be worse than leaving the range open.
# pyproject.toml bounds both at the next major.
#
# CAVEAT: this lock is not satisfiable on every interpreter pyproject.toml
# allows. scipy 1.18.0 -- pulled in by vectorbt -- requires >=3.12, so on 3.11
# resolve the ranges instead of applying the lock. Only 3.14 is a tested,
# reproducible target; CI byte-compiles the rest.

# --- direct: declared in pyproject.toml -------------------------------------
